selected_problem: Fresh-main reality testing found the POSIX timeout process-tree fallback could be cancelled when the shell closed before its stubborn descendant. A descendant that ignored SIGTERM/SIGHUP and redirected inherited stdio let runCommand return a timed-out receipt while the descendant remained alive and performed a late filesystem write.

decision_provenance.mode_route_basis: The committed four-mode router selects DEEP_DEVELOPMENT through the singular evidence-rich central bottleneck gate; no mode rotation was forced.
decision_provenance.claim_limit: No hosted DWAC success receipt is claimed. Selection/routing use committed DWAC source-contract replay over fresh canonical main while the provider remained transiently unavailable.

pre_fix_reproduction.scenario: A background Node descendant installs SIGTERM/SIGHUP handlers, redirects stdout/stderr away from the shell pipes, writes a ready marker, schedules a late filesystem write, while the shell waits. runCommand uses containProcessTree=true and timeoutMs=400.
pre_fix_reproduction.observed: The shell closed around 419ms after timeout, runCommand returned immediately and cleared the scheduled SIGKILL fallback; the stubborn descendant survived and wrote late.txt roughly one second after start.

changes: runCommand can probe whether its POSIX process group still exists after the shell close event.
When a timeout/output-limit stop is active and the contained process group is still alive, the command receipt is held instead of cancelling the SIGKILL fallback.
The bounded SIGKILL fallback now completes the containment barrier before a closed-shell receipt is resolved.
If the process group is already gone, runCommand still resolves without waiting for the grace timer.
Persistent interactive terminal semantics remain unchanged.
A focused regression proves a stubborn descendant cannot perform a late write after runCommand returns its timed-out receipt.

validation.tests: 15/15 PASS; 0 skipped on the POSIX validation host

truth_boundaries: The completion barrier is reality-verified for POSIX process-group containment; equivalent Windows descendant-tree containment remains unresolved.
The grace interval is bounded and may delay a timed-out receipt while stubborn descendants are being force-terminated; this is intentional to preserve the no-late-effects containment claim.
This is not an OS-level filesystem/network sandbox and does not prevent effects that occur before timeout/termination begins.
Arbitrary complex repository semantic synthesis remains UNRESOLVED.
Filesystem crash-level atomicity for arbitrary I/O/process failure remains unresolved.
No GitHub Actions were intentionally triggered or rerun, no force push was used, and no credential, payment, formal Release or destructive/irreversible external action was performed.
